title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1965 notes on the 'Galois theory of motives'. A category of motives over a base (written X or T, of finite type over Z) is to be a 'catégorie galoisienne' (Grothendieck's early name for a Tannakian category). Each point of the base supplies a realization (fibre) functor, and the motivic Galois group at that point is the group of tensor automorphisms of that fibre functor.

(1) Archimedean points, first paragraph. Let x vary over complex points (complex archimedean places). For a complex point x, Betti realization with integral coefficients gives an affine group scheme pi_{x,Z}. For a real point x, one gets pi_{x,R}, which Grothendieck identifies with pi_{x,C} equipped with tau, the involution induced by complex conjugation. This is the analogue of a decomposition group carrying a 'real Frobenius' F_infinity.
- He first conjectures that the pi_{x,Z} and pi_{x,R} attached to distinct places are pairwise non-isomorphic.
- He adds that the pi_{x,C} = pi_{x,infinity} are isomorphic to one another, but not canonically.
- A circled marginal note corrects this: 'faux, cf groupoïde fondamental sur Z'. Read this way, the isomorphisms between fibre functors at different points are governed by a fundamental groupoid over Z. One should therefore think in terms of torsors of paths between points, not of isolated groups, and the non-isomorphism claim is withdrawn.

(2) Real points, the NB. He writes 'T_x(R) = empty' (reading uncertain) and links this to two things: the 'connected components' phenomenon and 'ramification at R'. In modern terms these are the role of pi_0 of the real locus and of complex places lying over real ones, i.e. archimedean ramification with tau as inertia/Frobenius. The paragraph breaks off ('considérons alors... Si').

(3) Left margin. 'vérifier s'il n'y a pas d'analogue en grand des pts à val. dans une cat. t[ann?]...' Read plausibly, this asks whether there is a large-scale analogue of points with values in a (Tannakian?) tensor category, i.e. fibre functors valued in a tensor category other than Vec_k.

(4) Bottom section, systematized. An arithmetic point of X with values in a field (or ring) k is a point xi of T(k). The fibre of a motive at such a point gives a fibre functor; with tensor product, these form a 'catégorie galoisienne'. For fixed k, the isomorphisms from one point xi in T(k) to another form a torsor (the text breaks off at 'forment le'). This is the motivic fundamental groupoid: path torsors Isom^⊗(omega_xi, omega_eta) under the motivic Galois groups.
errors: The claim that the pi_{x,Z}, pi_{x,R} at distinct places are non-isomorphic is retracted by Grothendieck himself ('faux, cf groupoïde fondamental sur Z'). Groups at different fibre functors are inner twists of one another by the Isom torsor, so asserting non-isomorphism without analysing that torsor is unjustified.

'T_x(R) = empty' is ambiguous and probably partly misread. As stated it would contradict having real points x; it more likely concerns a specific space of real 'paths' or points, which the page leaves unclear.
Mixing integral Betti coefficients (Z) with a Tannakian formalism is delicate: over Z one needs Tannakian theory over a Dedekind base (Saavedra, Wedhorn), which the page does not address.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group at a point: tensor automorphisms of the realization fibre functor at a complex/real point, with integral coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group (Tannakian group of motives) relative to the Betti fibre functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjectural framework), formalized by Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne–Milne (1982)
ideas.where_published: Mentioned in Récoltes et Semailles as part of the 'yoga des motifs'; written up by Saavedra (LNM 265)

ideas.what: Real place as complex fibre functor plus the involution tau (complex conjugation)
ideas.modern_name: Real Frobenius F_infinity / real structure on Betti realization; motivic Galois group over R with Gal(C/R) action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Valeurs de fonctions L, 1979; Hodge II/III), Serre

ideas.what: Isomorphisms between fibre functors at different points form torsors: a fundamental groupoid of motives over Z
ideas.modern_name: Motivic fundamental groupoid / path torsors between fibre functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points, 1989; Catégories tannakiennes, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and the Faltings letter discuss fundamental groupoids with base points, though not motivic torsors in this form

ideas.what: Archimedean 'ramification' and connected components of real points as the arithmetic phenomenon at real places
ideas.modern_name: Archimedean places in Arakelov/arithmetic topology; pi_0 of X(R) and real section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various (Artin–Verdier, Cox, Mochizuki/Pál for real section conjecture)

ideas.what: Points with values in a tensor/Tannakian category ('analogue en grand')
ideas.modern_name: Fibre functors with values in a general tensor category (e.g. Rep or super-vector spaces)

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins treating archimedean places on the same footing as finite places in the motivic Galois picture: pi_{x,R} as pi_{x,C} with tau, 'ramification en R', connected components. He then retracts the non-isomorphism claim in favour of a fundamental groupoid over Z. The integral groupoid comparing all places, archimedean included, is left undeveloped.
missed.quote: les pi_{x,Z} et les pi_{x,R} [≃ pi_{x,C} muni de tau] qui correspondent à des places distinctes sont non isomorphes ... faux, cf groupoïde fondamental sur Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral motivic groupoids that include archimedean places relate to current work on Arakelov motives and to the real/archimedean section conjecture. The idea is suggestive, but only at the level of a sketch.

missed.claim: A 1965 query on 'points with values in a tensor category' anticipates Deligne's fibre functors valued in arbitrary tensor categories.
missed.quote: vérifier s'il n'y a pas d'analogue en grand des pt à val. dans une cat. t...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest as an early trace of the idea. The reading of the margin is uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early (1965) trace of the motivic fundamental groupoid as torsors between fibre functors at arithmetic points, including a real place modeled as pi_C with complex conjugation. This predates Deligne's 1989 treatment, but it is consistent with the known Grothendieck–Saavedra programme. The content is fragmentary, partly self-retracted, and largely illegible, so there is no new finished result.
transcription_corrections: '{+Kant [?]+}' is likely a crossed-out or inserted word (possibly 'non canoniquement' or 'Kummer'), not 'Kant'.
Left margin likely reads 'vérifier s'il n'y a pas d'analogue en grand des pt à val. dans une cat. t[ann./ens.] ??? vieille'.
Bottom: 'Le gr. de C' likely 'Les foncteurs fibres' or 'Le groupe de Galois'; 'forment une catégorie galoisienne ... muni de ⊗, c'est un [schéma en groupes?]'.
'gr fondamental' in the circled margin reads 'groupoïde fondamental sur Z'.
